correctness.rationale: Proposition 7.1 and Appendix B of arXiv:2610.01276v1 give the 24 base parameters, their fourth-root parameters, and the node coordinates. Appendix A gives the six relevant section formulas. An exact Q(i)-arithmetic replay verifies all 96 node parameters, evaluates every one of the six section images at every node, and obtains incidence multiplicities 44,24,16,8,4 for multiplicities 1 through 5, with 32 nodes on each section. The multiplicity-one nodes are distributed 6,6,10,6,6,10, so each section has a node on no other candidate; this directly proves that no proper subset covers all 96 nodes. An exhaustive subset check independently returns minimum cover size 6.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper proves coverage and records one witness section per node, but does not give the full six-by-96 incidence relation or a minimality theorem for the chosen six centers. The exact complete incidence computation is not implied by the one-witness table: several nodes lie on multiple selected section images, and one must test all six formulas at every node to determine whether any center is redundant. Targeted database and web searches found no covering statement.
residual_risks: The claim is deliberately relative to the six explicit section images; an alternative family of divisors could conceivably cover the nodes with fewer centers.
A complete incidence matrix could exist in unpublished computations not exposed in the inspected source materials.

value.rationale: The six section divisors are the global mechanism that turns Burek's nodal Weierstrass model into a projective crepant resolution. Determining whether all six are genuinely needed is therefore a natural structural question about the construction rather than an arbitrary finite statistic. The answer is sharp: 44 nodes are private to one selected section, and every section owns private nodes. This certifies that the published six-center strategy contains no redundant center within its explicit section family and supplies the full incidence profile for future comparisons of alternative resolutions.
